description: Ex-British Overseas Airways Corporation airliner displayed outdoors in false Royal Air Force markings as XM497. Part of the former British Airways collection.
Ex-Royal Danish Air Force Catalina displayed outdoors. Reported as deteriorating in the open and in need of indoor accommodation.
Ex-No. 32 Squadron, flown in from RAF Northolt in 1994; maintenance serial 9241M. Displayed outdoors as of August 2026 although the museum's web entry still shows it in Hangar 1.
Ex-No. 3 Flying Training School navigation trainer coded M, flown in from RAF Cranwell in 2011; displayed outdoors.
Ex-No. 51 Squadron signals intelligence aircraft, flown to Kemble in 2011 and delivered to Cosford by road in 2012; displayed outdoors.
Ex-No. 47 Squadron Hercules coded 202, flown in from RAF Brize Norton in 2011; displayed outdoors.
aliases: C130K; C-130K; Hercules C3; Hercules C.3; C130

description: Ex-Royal Netherlands Navy Neptune displayed outdoors. Reported in 2025 as scheduled for disposal, so presence should be re-checked before a visit.
aliases: SP2H; SP-2H; P-2; Neptune; SP2; P2

description: Ex-No. 101 Squadron transport and tanker named Bob Hope, wearing squadron 95th anniversary markings; displayed outdoors.
aliases: VC-10; VC10 C1K; Bob Hope; VC10

description: Gate guardian at the museum entrance in No. 237 Operational Conversion Unit markings; maintenance serial 8713M. Confirmed in place August 2026.
Displayed outdoors in No. 50 Squadron markings; previously inside Hangar 1. Confirmed outside August 2026 although it no longer appears on the museum's collection web pages.
Royal Aircraft Establishment marked Varsity, maintenance serial 9155M, standing outdoors. Offered for transfer in the museum's 2025 disposals programme, so its future at Cosford is uncertain.
The first prototype Jet Provost, maintenance serial 7570M, standing outdoors. Listed in the museum's 2025 disposals programme.
Coded Y, maintenance serial 8078M; standing outdoors. No longer listed on the museum's collection web pages.
Fuselage only, coded 38 in No. 1 Flying Training School markings; standing outdoors.
Ex-Royal Air Force of Oman Hunter wearing Omani serial 853; stored outdoors and not part of the indoor display.
Ex-No. 45 Squadron multi-engine trainer coded D. Held outdoors away from the indoor galleries; the museum's web entry still shows it in Hangar 1.
The second TSR-2 built and one of only two surviving airframes; never flown. Centrepiece of the Test Flight hangar. Maintenance serial 7933M.
The only surviving complete Boulton Paul Defiant, displayed in the markings EW-D of No. 307 (Polish) Squadron; maintenance serial 8370M.
Full-size replica of the Bristol M.1c monoplane scout in No. 150 Squadron markings; it is a reproduction, not an original airframe.
The Experimental Aircraft Programme demonstrator that led to the Eurofighter Typhoon; displayed in the Test Flight hangar.
Fairey Delta 2 research aircraft, the second built; maintenance serial 7986M. Sister aircraft WG774 took the world air speed record in 1956.
Complete Gladiator I in No. 247 Squadron markings, displayed in the Test Flight hangar.
Hart Trainer recovered from instructional use, displayed in No. 2 Flying Training School markings.
aliases: Hart II; Hart IIA; Hawker Hart

description: Displayed coded UH-A in No. 1682 Bomber Defence Training Flight markings; maintenance serial 5405M.
Tripartite Evaluation Squadron vertical take-off research aircraft coded 5, ancestor of the Harrier; naval instructional number A2619.

Black 6, Werknummer 10639, captured in North Africa in 1942 and given the RAF serial RN228; restored to flight and grounded after a 1997 accident. The RAF Museum's Bf 109G is at the Midlands site, not at Hendon.
Original Royal Naval Air Service Sopwith Pup, later civil G-APUP; displayed in the Test Flight hangar.
Full-size reproduction built in the 1980s and marked for No. 45 Squadron Royal Flying Corps; it is a replica, not an original airframe.
The oldest surviving Spitfire, the 155th built, displayed coded SD-D in No. 72 Squadron markings; maintenance serial 8383M.
The Active Control Technology fly-by-wire Jaguar demonstrator, displayed in the Test Flight hangar.
Elementary trainer wearing the false serial T9707; later civil G-AKKR and maintenance serial 8378M. Confirmed indoors August 2026 although the museum's web entry places it in the closed Hangar 1.
aliases: Magister I; Miles M.14A; M14A; G-AKKR

description: The only complete Avro Lincoln in the United Kingdom, ex-No. 151 Squadron at RAF Watton; displayed in the War in the Air hangar.

One of only two surviving Wellingtons. Restored by the Michael Beetham Conservation Centre and moved into the main display hangars fully assembled in 2023; it is now the centrepiece of the Strike Hard Strike Sure Bomber Command exhibition and is on public view.
Canadian-built Bolingbroke IVT restored and presented as a Blenheim IV coded XD-E; a recent arrival in the Bomber Command exhibition.
Ex-No. 3 Civilian Anti-Aircraft Co-operation Unit target tug, displayed coded AZ-E; maintenance serial 7806M.
Elementary trainer, maintenance serial 8387M, displayed in the War in the Air hangar.
Werknummer 733682, captured in Denmark in May 1945 and given the British evaluation number AM75; the upper component of a Mistel composite.
Ex-Indian Air Force Tempest II displayed coded OQ-H in the War in the Air hangar.
Werknummer 360043, coded D5+EV; defected to Dyce near Aberdeen in May 1943 with its Lichtenstein radar intact and given the RAF serial PJ876.
Werknummer 112372, yellow 4; captured and given the RAF serial VK893 for evaluation.
Hornisse heavy fighter coded 3U+CC, the only surviving example. The museum's collection entry records it as not currently on display.
Nose section only, displayed indoors.
aliases: C47; C-47; Dakota III; DC-3; DC3

description: Storch liaison aircraft on display at Cosford since 1989 and listed in the museum's 2025 disposals programme; its display status is uncertain and it is not shown on the current collection web pages.
V-1 flying bomb displayed in the War in the Air hangar.
German Army V-2 ballistic missile, assembly 4, displayed in the War in the Air hangar.
German long-range artillery rocket displayed in the War in the Air hangar.
Ex-No. 44 Squadron; airborne reserve for the Black Buck Falklands raids in 1982. Maintenance serial 8778M. Suspended in the National Cold War Exhibition.
Maid Marian, ex-No. 55 Squadron, the last Victor to fly; maintenance serial 9242M. Displayed in the National Cold War Exhibition. Note that Victor XH563 is not part of this collection.
The only surviving complete Valiant; dropped Britain's first hydrogen bomb during Operation Grapple in 1957 with No. 49 Squadron. Maintenance serial 7894M.
Early production Lightning, sometimes quoted as a P.1B; maintenance serial 8056M. Suspended in the National Cold War Exhibition.
The oldest surviving Javelin; maintenance serial 7464M. Displayed in the National Cold War Exhibition.
Ex-No. 39 Squadron photographic reconnaissance Canberra coded U; maintenance serial 8746M.
Enceladus, coded 371, ex-No. 53 Squadron; the largest aircraft in the collection and the centrepiece of the National Cold War Exhibition.
aliases: Belfast C1; Enceladus; Short SC.5; SC5

description: Bombing trainer conversion coded 511; maintenance serial 8554M.

Maintenance serial 8442M, ex-No. 6 Flying Training School at RAF Finningley. Moved out of the closed Hangar 1 and displayed in the National Cold War Exhibition; the museum's web entry still shows it in Hangar 1.
aliases: Argosy C1; Argosy T1; AW.660; AW660

description: Night fighter coded J in No. 264 Squadron markings; maintenance serial 7937M.
Ex-civil G-AGNV; the only complete Avro York, displayed in the National Cold War Exhibition.
Canadian-built F-86 Sabre in No. 93 Squadron markings coded U.

Two-seat Hunter coded X in No. 74 Squadron markings; maintenance serial 9224M.
Nose section only; maintenance serials 7762M and 8585M.
Nose section only, wearing the false identity XN972; maintenance serial 8183M. The museum's collection entry records it as not currently on display.
Nose section only, coded 013, displayed in the National Cold War Exhibition.
Ex-Polish Air Force Lim-2, displayed in the National Cold War Exhibition; the serial is also quoted as 1120.
Ex-Hungarian Air Force interceptor; also recorded wearing the number 503.
Coded P-C in No. 1 Flying Training School markings; maintenance serial 7606M. Moved out of the closed Hangar 1 into the National Cold War Exhibition.
United States Air Force Pave Low special operations helicopter; also quoted as an MH-53J.
aliases: MH53M; MH-53M; MH-53J; Pave Low; MH53; MH53J

description: No. 22 Squadron search and rescue markings; maintenance serial 8726M. Confirmed at Cosford in November 2025 although the museum's web entry places it at the London site.
Air defence Tornado coded GF in No. 43 Squadron markings; recorded on display indoors in December 2024. Not shown on the museum's collection web pages.
Intermediate range ballistic missile of the kind deployed in Britain from 1958; displayed in the National Cold War Exhibition.
Air-launched ballistic missile cancelled in 1962; displayed in the National Cold War Exhibition.
Submarine-launched ballistic missile of the British deterrent; displayed in the National Cold War Exhibition.
Stand-off nuclear missile carried by the V-bombers; displayed in the National Cold War Exhibition.
Surface to air missile that defended the V-bomber airfields; displayed in the National Cold War Exhibition.
Army surface to air missile displayed in the National Cold War Exhibition.
Low level air defence missile displayed in the National Cold War Exhibition.
Tracked launcher version of the Rapier air defence system.
Infra-red guided air to air missile carried by the Lightning and Sea Vixen.
Short Range Air to Air Missile technology demonstrator.
Early Sidewinder air to air missile.
Sparrow semi-active radar homing air to air missile.
Anti-radar version of the Anglo-French Martel missile.
Lightweight helicopter-launched anti-ship missile.
Wire-guided anti-tank missile displayed in the National Cold War Exhibition.
Australian anti-tank missile displayed in the National Cold War Exhibition.
Chinese Silkworm or Seersucker anti-ship missile.

Mixed rocket and jet powered interceptor prototype, one of two built. Held in the Michael Beetham Conservation Centre, which is an engineering workshop rarely open to visitors except during its annual open week. Reported in 2025 as awaiting a new home.

Jet-flap research aircraft flown by the Royal Aircraft Establishment. Held in the Michael Beetham Conservation Centre, which is an engineering workshop rarely open to visitors except during its annual open week. Reported in 2025 as awaiting a new home.
Coded G and named Sunshine in No. 72 Squadron markings. Held in the Michael Beetham Conservation Centre, which is an engineering workshop rarely open to visitors except during its annual open week.

Queen's Flight VIP Gazelle in No. 32 Squadron markings. Survivor records place it at the Beetham Centre at Cosford in August 2026, while the museum's own web entry and published lists still show it on display at Hendon; needs checking on site.
aliases: Gazelle HCC4; Gazelle HT3; SA.341; SA341

description: Central Flying School Bulldog coded 3. Held in the Michael Beetham Conservation Centre, which is an engineering workshop rarely open to visitors except during its annual open week.

Falklands veteran coded V in No. 4 Squadron markings; maintenance serial 9122M. Held in the Michael Beetham Conservation Centre, which is an engineering workshop rarely open to visitors except during its annual open week.

Bravo November, the Falklands and multi-campaign veteran whose crews won four Distinguished Flying Crosses; retired to the museum in 2022. Held in the Michael Beetham Conservation Centre, which is an engineering workshop rarely open to visitors except during its annual open week. It has appeared in the open at the Cosford Air Show.

The only surviving Dornier Do 17, coded 5K+AR, recovered from the Goodwin Sands in 2013. A wing is shown inside the Conservation Centre and the fuselage is in store; conservation is long-term and it is not a normal gallery exhibit.

First World War German two-seater, works number 7198/18 and later civil G-AANJ. Fabric removed and structural survey complete; future plans undecided. Held in the Michael Beetham Conservation Centre, which is an engineering workshop rarely open to visitors except during its annual open week.
Wreckage only, recovered from the sea; held in store and not on public view. Distinct from the complete Defiant N1671 displayed in the Test Flight hangar.
Ex-South African Air Force 6130. Listed in the museum's 2025 disposals programme. Held in the museum's reserve store at Cosford and not on public view.
The oldest surviving Meteor airframe, a prototype F.9/40 carrying the G suffix. Held in the museum's reserve store at Cosford and not on public view.
Fuselage only, the sole surviving Brigand. Held in the museum's reserve store at Cosford and not on public view.
The first P.1A research aircraft, ancestor of the Lightning; maintenance serial 7755M. Held in the museum's reserve store at Cosford and not on public view.
Naval Balliol trainer; a transfer to the Fleet Air Arm Museum has been proposed. Held in the museum's reserve store at Cosford and not on public view.
Maintenance serial 7998M. Held in the museum's reserve store at Cosford and not on public view.

Stainless steel high-speed research aircraft, the second of two built; maintenance serial 8368M. Reported in 2025 as hoped to transfer to Aerospace Bristol. Held in the museum's reserve store at Cosford and not on public view.

Short take-off communications aircraft wearing the false serial XL554 in Sultan of Oman's Air Force markings; maintenance serial 8034M. Held in the museum's reserve store at Cosford and not on public view.
Prototype Tornado coded WT; maintenance serial 8883M. Held in the museum's reserve store at Cosford and not on public view.

Argentine ground attack aircraft captured in the Falklands in 1982 and given the British serial ZD485; listed in the museum's 2025 disposals programme. Held in the museum's reserve store at Cosford and not on public view.
Ex-Red Arrows Hawk acquired in 2026; shown at the Cosford Air Show in June 2026 and then placed in store pending the new 1980 to Today exhibition.
aliases: Hawk T1A; Hawk T1; Red Arrows

description: Ex-No. 13 Squadron Reaper, UK08-117, retired in 2025 and acquired by the museum in 2026; shown at the Cosford Air Show in June 2026 and then placed in store.
